Kaise Main Likhon Shan Teri Shah-e-Khurasan
Hai Madha Yeh Quran Teri Shah-e-Khurasan.

1
Jab Parh Ke Khatam Karta Hoon karta Hai Sana Phir.
Woh Sorah-e-Rehman Teri Shah-e-Khurasan.
Har Cheez Mein Tujh Se Hi Tu Mangoon Ga Aye Mula.
Hai Dolat-e-Yazdan Teri Shah-e-Khurasan.

2
Akbar Ki Tu Jageer Hai Woh Karb-o-Bala Par.
Jageer Hai Iran Teri Shah-e-Khurasan.
Nokar Ne Tere Roka Hai Tofan-e-Samandar.
Kafi Hai Yehi Shan Teri Shah-e-Khurasan.

3
Hoti Hai Atta Zindagi Darbar Se Tere.
Khud Maut Hai Darban Teri Shah-e-Khurasan.
Zawwar Yeh Afraz Tera Sab Se Hai Kehta.
Janat Hai Khurasan Teri Shah-e-Khurasan.

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/kaise-main-likhon-shan-teri-shah-e-khurasan-lyrics-2018-tajpoints-ed295bbbeb9f05ed5a03.md')
s = p.read_text()
_, metadata, body = s.split('---', 2)
roman = metadata.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1]
for edition, numbers in [(roman, '123'), (body, '۱۲۳')]:
    blocks = edition.strip().split('\\n\\n')
    assert [len(b.splitlines()) for b in blocks] == [2, 5, 5, 5]
    assert [b.splitlines()[0].strip() for b in blocks[1:]] == list(numbers)
assert '\\u200c' not in s
print('Both editions contain a two-verse opening and three four-verse stanzas.')
PY"

Reconstructed all 14 verses in Urdu script and moved the Roman transcription to `romanLyrics`, preserving its wording and order. Verified that both versions have a two-verse opening and three four-verse stanzas.

Set the Urdu title and right-to-left direction, removed `noUrdu`, and kept the poem title in Roman as `alternateTitle`, omitting the “Lyrics 2018” suffix. I read “Madha” as مدح and “Afraz” as افراز. Only the selected lyric was edited.
